# Reader

> Personal research library for turning saved articles and PDFs into focused reading, annotation, retrieval, and source-grounded discussion.

## When to use this

- Use Reader when a web article or PDF deserves attentive reading and durable notes.
- Use Reader when a claim should remain close to the passage and annotation behind it.
- Do not treat Reader as a source-verification service; it preserves material but does not validate its claims.
- Do not expect public social reading, real-time collaboration, or paid team workflows.

## Current state

- Mature personal-use product in maintenance-first support.
- Browser-local start; Google sign-in for the account-backed library.
- Libraries are private by default; sharing is explicit.
- Chrome extension is source-built for local unpacked use, not publicly distributed.
- No public plan or checkout; no permanent pricing model is declared.

## Agent guidance

- Personal libraries and authenticated APIs are private and are not agent-indexed.
- The public OpenAPI document describes discovery surfaces, not an unauthenticated library API.
- Use the Reader source workflow to decide whether a source belongs in this product and to guide a human through the capture-to-reading loop.
